Hamina, the sequel to Doodle 6 Trade Secret: the regulator (LVV) asked Google's Finnish company to pause expansion work at the Hamina data-centre site after conservationists said flying-squirrel routes were at risk; Google says it paused; LVV is examining the nature conservation act. argument: At Google's Hamina data-centre site, conservationists said the expansion work put flying squirrels' routes at risk; the regulator asked for a pause, Google paused, and the regulator is examining the nature conservation act.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word

text.en: Flying squirrels / live by Google's / [Hamina] site.

captions.source: Flying squirrel (liito-orava) habitat at the Hamina data-centre site is documented: HS and Yle (Oct 2026) report that about 1.3 ha of flying-squirrel forest was felled there without a permit in 2018-19, and the authority's own detailed-plan drawing marks the areas not to be felled (see papercut/trade-secret/copy.json). The present case is about the squirrels' movement routes (kulkuyhteydet) at the expansion site (Yle; Kymen Sanomat, Nov 2026). 'Around' rather than 'in' because the routes and the habitat run through and beside the site. Verified from search summaries only.

text.en: Conservationists / warned: their / [route] was at risk.

captions.source: Kymen Sanomat (first to report), then Yle and STT, about 4 Nov 2026: the local association of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation (Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto, its Kaakkois-Kymi association per the summaries) made an urgent request to LVV: the flying squirrels' movement routes may have been endangered, with earthworks and tree removal on the site. Attributed ('said'): it is their claim, which LVV is examining. Verified from search summaries only.

Yle (yle.fi/a/74-20254899), confirmed by email with LVV's environment department: LVV asked Tuike Finland (Google's Finnish company) to pause the expansion work at the Hamina data-centre site until the matter is resolved; press reports date the request 23 Oct 2026. 'Asked' because LVV's step is a request (pyysi), not an order; Maaseudun Tulevaisuus's headline says LVV 'halted' the felling. Google is named because Google's own statement speaks for the site (owner, 3 Nov: 'use Google for the Finland data centers'). Verified from search summaries only.

Google, quoted by Yle and Kymen Sanomat: 'olemme keskeyttaneet tyot Haminassa, jotta voimme keskustella LVV:n kanssa' (we have paused work in Hamina so we can talk with LVV); Tuike Finland said it agreed to the pause. The tag gives the next step: LVV has begun an urgent examination of whether Tuike Finland acted against the nature conservation act, in particular how the flying squirrels' routes were taken into account (Yle, yle.fi/a/74-20255224). Verified from search summaries only. v2 (6 Nov): Google's side on screen as the shot-4 tag: Google says the flying squirrels were taken into account and a 30 m wooded corridor is kept across the area (Yle; Kymen Sanomat; Uutissuomalainen papers, per search summaries, 6 Nov 17:16 check). LVV's step moves to a tag at the start of shot 5: LVV has opened an urgent inquiry (kiireellinen selvitys) into how the corridors were handled under the nature conservation act, and may send inspectors after hearing Tuike (Yle). The conservationists' claim is that the corridor risks being cut over ~50 m; not on screen (one figure from summaries, and two different measures side by side would confuse).

The station's line, a metaphor for the pause: the work stopped where the squirrels cross. Not a claim about any ruling; LVV's examination is open. The tag recalls the same site's history: about 1.3 ha of flying-squirrel forest felled without a permit in 2018-19 (HS, Yle; Doodle 6 Trade Secret).

post.en: Hamina, Finland: conservationists said Google's data-center work put a flying-squirrel route at risk. The regulator asked for a pause and opened an inquiry. Google paused; it says a 30 m corridor stays. In 2018–19, 1.3 ha of squirrel forest was cut without a permit. Right of way?
